abstract: Rab GTPases are the master players in the cellular transport system, but their function and regulation in cargo recruitment to COPII vesicles at the endoplasmic reticulum (ER) are unknown. Here, we demonstrate that Rab29 inhibition via genetic deletion and inactivation markedly impedes the ER-to-Golgi transport, cell surface expression, and cellular functions of a subset of G protein-coupled receptors (GPCRs). More interestingly, Rab29 inhibition substantially attenuates GPCR concentration and recruitment kinetics at ER-derived COPII vesicles without affecting vesicle biogenesis. We also show that activated Rab29 localizes to the ER and COPII vesicles where it directly interacts with both its cargo GPCRs and all four Sec24 isoforms. We further identify a specific motif that mediates the interaction of angiotensin II type 2 receptor (AT2R) with Rab29; mutating this motif effectively blocks AT2R recruitment into COPII vesicles and compromises its delivery to the cell surface. Collectively, these data indicate that Rab29 is the first Rab functioning as a specific cargo transport receptor to enhance COPII capture and anterograde trafficking of GPCRs from the ER which is mediated through activation-dependent interactions with both Sec24 and cargo GPCRs and identify a novel function for the Rab family in membrane trafficking.

summary: Rab29 acts as a cargo receptor that recruits GPCRs into COPII vesicles at the ER, promoting their anterograde trafficking to the cell surface.
